causal_model: Pandemic gains were driven predominantly by ticket rather than volume; normalization could expose a second leg down after FY2023 guidance.
claim_text: Morris questioned whether FY2023 would be a durable base or whether another deterioration leg remained.
evidence_quote: whether FY23 is a base for The Home Depot to build off of ... or if there’s another shoe to drop
outcome: FY2023 sales fell 3.0% and comps fell 3.2%; FY2024 core comps remained negative, though acquired SRS revenue lifted total sales.
conflicts: Paid research subscription; public position disclosure was not visible on the accessible post.
notes: The question was framed conditionally, so the outcome is mixed rather than a scored point forecast.

causal_model: Low housing affordability, falling existing-home sales and a renovation hangover from 2020-2022 would pressure discretionary projects and comps.
claim_text: Morris expected a difficult year or two and questioned whether Home Depot's FY2023 assumptions were still optimistic.
evidence_quote: it seems reasonable to assume that a more difficult year or two lies ahead
outcome: FY2023 sales fell 3.0% and comps fell 3.2%; FY2024 comparable sales fell 1.8% even as acquisitions lifted reported sales.
conflicts: Paid research subscription; public position disclosure was not visible on the accessible post.
notes: This is the cleanest public Morris falsifiable direction call in the target window.

causal_model: Brand equity, scale, omnichannel merchandising and a fragmented market should sustain modest share gains despite near-term housing pressure.
claim_text: Morningstar projected 2.4% average sales growth and 1.9% average comparable-sales growth over five years.
evidence_quote: We project 2.4% average sales growth over the next five years, supported by 1.9% average same-store sales increases
outcome: Only FY2024 and FY2025 are reported; acquisition-heavy total-sales growth makes the five-year organic thesis premature to score.
conflicts: Institutional research product; methodology and disclosures are available, but model detail is partly paywalled.
notes: Keep open until the full horizon; do not infer accuracy from the stock price.

causal_model: SRS adds sales and Pro reach, but its purchase multiple, debt funding and interest expense offset much of the incremental value.
claim_text: Katz and Grace Na called the SRS price slightly rich and expected minimal change to Morningstar's $263 fair value.
evidence_quote: the $18.25 billion price tag ... strikes us as a touch rich
outcome: SRS contributed $6.4 billion of FY2024 sales and Home Depot continued the specialty-distribution strategy; value creation remains unseasoned.
conflicts: Institutional research product; coauthored with Grace Na.
notes: The public page provides a differentiated acquisition model, not merely a rating.

causal_model: An 80% second-quarter contribution and full second-half consolidation of SRS should add about $9 billion sales and $500 million EBITDA to the 2024 model.
claim_text: Katz added roughly $9 billion of 2024 sales and $500 million of EBITDA for SRS and raised fair value to $270.
evidence_quote: raising our 2024 sales outlook by roughly $9 billion and our EBITDA by around $500 million
outcome: Home Depot disclosed $6.4 billion of SRS sales for seven months but did not publish standalone SRS FY2024 EBITDA on the same forecast basis.
conflicts: Institutional research product.
notes: Do not compare the $9 billion model increment directly with $6.4 billion actual without reconciling consolidation timing and model baseline.

causal_model: Lower mortgage rates unlock frozen housing turnover, which then releases deferred large-project home-improvement demand.
claim_text: Nagel argued that lower rates would unlock housing paralysis and drive better Home Depot sales.
evidence_quote: Lower rates will help to unlock that paralysis and serve as a driver of better sales at Home Depot
outcome: Fiscal 2025 comparable sales rose only 0.3%; the conditional rate-and-turnover recovery case has not fully occurred.
conflicts: Sell-side analyst covering the company; full Oppenheimer research is not public.
notes: Useful causal mechanism; timing was not specified, so it cannot be marked missed.

causal_model: Housing-channel weakness and project deferral would persist beyond the quarter despite eventual rate relief.
claim_text: Nagel reiterated that sales weakness at Home Depot and across the channel would remain soft for longer.
evidence_quote: sales weakness at the chain and across the channel is likely to remain soft for a while longer
outcome: FY2024 comps declined 1.8%; FY2025 comps improved only 0.3%, consistent with a shallow, delayed recovery.
conflicts: Sell-side analyst; LinkedIn post promotes a CNBC appearance and underlying research is not public.
notes: Published date is visible in the LinkedIn activity identifier and aligns with the Q2 FY2024 report date.

causal_model: Existing-home turnover drives project demand; delayed rate cuts prolong weakness, while light projects face specialist competition and bargain shopping.
claim_text: Saunders identified the soft housing market as the chief constraint on Home Depot and saw narrowing prospects for a near-term rate-led lift.
evidence_quote: Home Depot’s current performance is chiefly affected by softness in the current soft housing market
outcome: Home Depot's FY2024 comparable sales declined 1.8%, while management continued to cite high rates and housing pressure.
conflicts: GlobalData sells retail intelligence; public comments are often distributed after earnings rather than before them.
notes: Industry-specialist causal interpretation, not an EPS estimate.

causal_model: DIY spending typically follows a home move by six to twelve months, so even late-2024 housing improvement would not help until well into 2025.
claim_text: Saunders expected any late-2024 housing pickup to reach DIY demand only well into 2025.
evidence_quote: the sweet spot for DIY spending is 6 months to a year after people have moved
outcome: FY2025 comps rose only 0.3%, with the strongest quarterly improvement arriving later in the year rather than immediately.
conflicts: GlobalData sells retail intelligence; quote is reported by Axios.
notes: The prediction is about timing, not magnitude.

causal_model: Home Depot's Pro exposure and execution would yield better quarterly comparable sales than Lowe's.
claim_text: Horvers expected Home Depot to outcomp Lowe's in Q4 FY2024.
evidence_quote: HD likely to outcomp LOW in 4Q
outcome: Home Depot comparable sales increased 0.8%; Lowe's comparable sales increased 0.2%.
conflicts: Sell-side analyst; public evidence is secondary reporting of a JPMorgan note.
notes: Clean win, but the public archive is too thin for archetype-level status.

causal_model: Recruiters are operationally geared to client confidence; deteriorating macro conditions can overwhelm apparently cheaper valuations.
claim_text: Slingo warned that it was still too soon to buy the dip in Hays and PageGroup.
evidence_quote: we worry that it might still be too soon to buy the dip
outcome: Hays FY2024 pre-exceptional operating profit fell 46% LFL to £105.1 million and the shares continued lower.
conflicts: Financial journalism product; no personal position disclosure was visible in the accessible article.
notes: A differentiated early caution before the steep FY2024 profit decline.

claim_text: Callan rated Hays Buy with a 125p target when the disclosure chart shows a roughly 101p market price.
evidence_quote: 17/07/2023 Tom Callan 101 125 Buy
outcome: By the 17 April 2024 revision, Hays was about 89p and the target was cut to 105p; the prior upside did not materialize.
conflicts: Sell-side research; the disclosure PDF does not expose the underlying thesis text.
notes: Included as a named multi-year revision history and a necessary bullish counterexample, not because a price target alone makes a thought leader.

causal_model: Consultant headcount reduction was a leading signal of weakening client demand and broader economic stress.
claim_text: Shah said Hays' consultant reduction raised broader economic concerns despite management's confident distributions.
evidence_quote: the reduction in the consultant headcount raises broader economic concerns
outcome: FY2024 net fees fell 12% LFL and pre-exceptional operating profit fell 46% LFL.
conflicts: Edison provides issuer-sponsored research in parts of its business; the accessible article does not state the engagement status for Hays.
notes: Good signal, but only one attributable public Hays call was found.

claim_text: Callan retained Buy but cut the Hays target to 105p from 125p when the shares were about 89p.
evidence_quote: 17/04/2024 Tom Callan 89 105 Buy
outcome: By 14 October 2024 the shares were about 85p and the target was cut again to 95p.
conflicts: Sell-side research; reasoning is not public in the disclosure chart.
notes: The revision history is transparent; the causal thesis is not.

causal_model: Recruitment is cyclical, but paying a recovery multiple before fee momentum turns leaves insufficient downside protection.
claim_text: Scott expected eventual cyclical improvement but judged Hays too expensive before the recovery had started.
evidence_quote: the share price is asking me to pay too much up-front for a recovery that hasn’t even started yet
outcome: FY2025 net fees fell 11% LFL and pre-exceptional operating profit fell 56% to £45.6 million.
conflicts: Subscription financial publication; Stockopedia reports disclose author positions when present, and no Hays position was stated in the accessible section.
notes: Strong valuation discipline rather than a precise earnings estimate.

claim_text: Callan retained Buy and cut the target to 95p when Hays traded near 85p.
evidence_quote: 14/10/2024 Tom Callan 85 95 Buy
outcome: By 20 February 2025 Hays was about 72p and the target was cut to 86p.
conflicts: Sell-side research; reasoning is not public in the disclosure chart.
notes: Third consecutive bullish revision lower.

causal_model: Rapidly falling consensus and heavy second-half weighting made the unchanged full-year expectation fragile despite an in-line first half.
claim_text: Simpson flagged that Hays still needed a heavily weighted second half to reach the 2.34p EPS consensus.
evidence_quote: this still leaves them with an H2 weighting to hit the 2.34p EPS consensus
outcome: Hays warned in June and reported FY2025 pre-exceptional EPS of 1.31p, well below the cited 2.34p consensus.
conflicts: Subscription financial publication; personal position was not stated in the accessible section.
notes: A concrete accounting-risk observation rather than an explicit point estimate.

claim_text: Callan retained Buy with an 86p target when Hays traded around 72p.
evidence_quote: 20/02/2025 Tom Callan 72 86 Buy
outcome: By 19 June 2025 the shares were about 63p; Investec changed to Hold with a 64p target.
conflicts: Sell-side research; reasoning is not public in the disclosure chart.
notes: The eventual Hold revision is evidence of updating, but only after repeated target cuts.

causal_model: AI and geopolitical pressure favor smaller, agile specialist recruiters over large organizations that change slowly.
claim_text: Collingwood questioned whether large recruiters were too slow to adapt and whether smaller agencies now had an edge.
evidence_quote: are the bigger players simply too slow to change?
outcome: Hays H1 FY2026 net fees fell 9% and operating profit fell 25%; this is consistent with pressure but does not isolate agility or AI causation.
conflicts: Runs a recruitment business that can benefit from a narrative favoring smaller agencies.
notes: Industry edge is meaningful; the post followed a profit warning, so it is thesis formation rather than a pre-warning call.

causal_model: Persistent weakness may reflect displacement of the generalist recruitment-consultant model, while intangible-heavy balance sheets offer weak downside protection.
claim_text: Simpson preferred niche recruiters with tangible downside protection over larger generalists such as Hays.
evidence_quote: current weakness represents a shift away from the typical recruitment consultant model
outcome: Hays H1 FY2026 net fees fell 9%, operating profit fell 25%, the dividend fell 84%, and the CEO departed.
conflicts: Subscription financial publication; personal position was not stated in the accessible section.
notes: Differentiated causal thesis, but the result cannot prove structural displacement by itself.

causal_model: Temp seasonality and cost cutting offered limited support, while collapsing earnings forecasts and permanent-hiring weakness dominated.
claim_text: Head maintained an AMBER/RED view and found only temp demand and cost savings positive.
evidence_quote: I’d struggle to describe today’s quarterly statement as upbeat
outcome: H1 FY2026 net fees fell 9%, pre-exceptional operating profit fell 25%, and the dividend fell 84%.
conflicts: Subscription financial publication; personal position was not stated in the accessible section.
notes: Short track record on Hays, but falsifiable near-term caution.

causal_model: Several years of sector underperformance require a structural explanation such as LinkedIn disintermediation, not only macro uncertainty.
claim_text: Neary argued that recruitment looked structurally broken and that macro conditions alone no longer explained the decline.
evidence_quote: there is something structurally broken with many recruitment companies, in my view
outcome: Hays subsequently began exiting noncore countries, but insufficient post-claim operating history exists to resolve the disintermediation thesis.
conflicts: Subscription financial publication; Stockopedia states Neary's positions where relevant and no Hays position was stated here.
notes: The most differentiated public Hays thesis found, but it is recent and unproven.

causal_model: Exiting low-return countries should reduce drag and improve group operational gearing when fees recover.
claim_text: Vidyarthi said the country exits should materially improve operational gearing and were the right action.
evidence_quote: These exits should materially improve the operational gearing of the business
outcome: The disposals are too recent for operating outcomes.
conflicts: Sell-side analyst; Panmure Liberum research is excerpted on public surfaces but full notes may require access.
notes: Useful named specialist view, but not yet a public multi-year thesis archive.

causal_model: AI automates commodity sourcing and screening; value shifts to specialist, advisory and technology-integrated staffing models.
claim_text: Watts argued that 2026 winners must treat recruitment pressure as structural rather than wait for a cyclical recovery.
evidence_quote: The firms that come out of 2026 in good shape will treat this as structural, not a cycle to wait out
outcome: No subsequent full-year results exist at the research cut.
conflicts: Advises staffing founders on growth and sale; structural-change framing can support demand for his services.
notes: Strong causal industry model and large public archive, but little pre-2026 Hays-specific history was found.
